title: Ala Singh and Patiala
hook: the Phulkian chiefs founded the states of Patiala, Nabha and Jind

segments.voice: Yesterday, Delhi, where Baghel Singh marked the places the Gurus had been. Your line was marking the places. Where did you stop for a breath? Today, a different kind of founding. Day eight hundred seventy-two.

A mud fort goes up on open ground in the Malwa country, south of the Sutlej. A well. A few houses around it. A market that starts with a handful of stalls. That's how some towns start, and Patiala, now a busy city in Indian Punjab, is remembered as starting something like that, around a fort built by a Sikh chief named Ala Singh. His family line had a name of its own, and a story that goes back to a Guru. Today: Ala Singh and Patiala.
screen: `A FORT ON OPEN GROUND.` → `A WELL, A FEW HOUSES, A MARKET.` → `THE TOWN THAT BECAME PATIALA.`

segments.voice: The family were the Phulkians, named for an ancestor called Phul. Phul means flower. And tradition tells a story about him as a small boy. He was brought, with his brother, before Guru Har Rai. The boys were hungry, and Phul patted his stomach. Tradition says the Guru took it as a sign and blessed him: his descendants would have enough, and would feed many. The Phulkian families remember that blessing as the root of what came after. That's the first piece. The second is what came after. Ala Singh, one of Phul's line, built up his holdings in these hard decades and founded the town and state of Patiala. Other branches of the same family founded the states of Nabha and Jind. So in the middle of the decades of persecution, some Sikh families were not only riding and hiding. They were laying out streets, digging wells, building forts and markets. The third piece is honesty. Ala Singh's story isn't a simple hero's tale. He dealt with more than one power to keep his state alive, and tradition records that this put him at odds at times with other Sikh leaders. This path tells it with that tension left in. The fourth piece is the small one. Every town you've lived in began somewhere: a crossing, a fort, a mill, a well. Someone chose that spot, and people kept coming. Towns begin.
screen: `PHUL: THE BOY THE GURU BLESSED.` · `PATIALA, NABHA AND JIND FOUNDED.` · `A FOUNDER'S STORY, TENSIONS LEFT IN.` · `EVERY TOWN BEGAN SOMEWHERE.` · then, large: `TOWNS BEGIN.`

segments.voice: For this sit, go to where your town began. Close your eyes, and breathe. Picture the place you live. Now take away the newest buildings, then the roads, then the wires, until you're looking at whatever was there first: a river crossing, a fort, a farm, a station, a church or a temple or a well. You may not know the real answer. That's fine. Wonder about it. Who chose that spot, and why? Who kept coming? If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out. The bell holds the time.
Patiala. The town and state founded by Ala Singh of the Phulkian line, the family tradition says Guru Har Rai blessed. Today's word.
